review_basis: Fellow-endorsed provisional directions; zero source-level approval unless separately recorded

provisional_cards.title: Why start a SIP, and what was expected?

working_reading.text: A new graduate describes a plan to organise investments, keep an emergency buffer and start SIP contributions. This is stated intention before starting, not evidence of an actual SIP or later outcome.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: An apparent starting expectation may have come from an adviser or creator rather than the investor.
provisional_cards.unknown: Starting expectations for the first-time Groww cohort remain unknown unless the investor states them.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Ask a first-SIP investor what they hoped the recurring payment would achieve and when they expected to notice progress; record who influenced that expectation.

provisional_cards.title: What changes after starting?

working_reading.text: The same writer describes a start followed by cancellation of the initial buy. That is one short sequence; it does not establish a change over later months or a stopped scheduled SIP.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: Different stages across different writers may resemble change within one person.
provisional_cards.unknown: A change needs at least two timepoints from the same investor; separate posts cannot make a trajectory.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Find one person describing their own starting month and a later month, including the changed circumstance, action and resulting payment state.

provisional_cards.title: What leads to pausing, reducing or stopping?

working_reading.text: An adjacent-platform writer reports two months when an intended mandate-funded SIP debit did not occur. The cause and later successful instalment are not confirmed.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: A missed payment may reflect a bank or mandate condition, a deliberate decision, or an unresolved status.
provisional_cards.unknown: A stated reason does not prove the payment system’s cause or a month-12 outcome.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Find an intended next instalment, the initiating event, what the investor did and whether that scheduled payment later succeeded; compare an informed pause.

provisional_cards.title: What do investors check, and how often?

working_reading.text: One experienced Paytm Money investor says they had not checked individual SIP transaction status, then checked after noticing rejected transactions and considered reviewing past transactions. This is one before-and-after checking account, not a frequency estimate for first-year Groww investors.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: People who post about checking may check more often than quiet investors.
provisional_cards.unknown: Checking frequency is unknown unless a person states a cadence and reference period.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Ask what the investor checked, the explicit checking cadence and the period that cadence covers; public posts without a cadence cannot answer frequency.

provisional_cards.title: What confuses or worries them in the app?

working_reading.text: A writer reports pausing then accidentally deleting one SIP and asks what happens to the holding. This shows a stated control question, while its later payment consequence remains unknown.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: The control may be available but hard to find, or the underlying payment status may be unclear.
provisional_cards.unknown: A documented control does not prove that investors noticed or understood it.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Find the exact SIP screen, message or control that was interpreted, what action followed and whether the app or an outside actor created the issue.

provisional_cards.title: What happens outside the app?

working_reading.text: In a follow-up to a Coin payment problem, the same poster reports using another UPI app and says current payments work. The later scheduled SIP outcome is not verified.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: A reply may suggest a workaround that the original writer never tried.
provisional_cards.unknown: Advice received, support contacted and action completed are different events.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Find a first-person sequence showing what help was sought outside the app, what was actually tried and whether the next SIP action worked.

provisional_cards.title: What differs between continuation and interruption?

working_reading.text: One writer reports roughly a year of SIP investing and considers increasing the amount. Their platform, first-ever MF status and a comparable difficult-month outcome are unknown.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: A continuation difference may reflect circumstances rather than the app experience.
provisional_cards.unknown: Public posts cannot reveal silent continuers or silent drop-offs, or establish a causal difference.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Pair a continuer and an interrupter who faced a comparable difficult month; record circumstances, protective cues and the next scheduled payment for both.

provisional_cards.title: How do circumstances differ across accounts?

working_reading.text: One pre-start writer explicitly mentions a new job, a planned emergency buffer and a support system. This describes one person’s circumstances; there is no observed SIP outcome or basis for a segment comparison.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: A visible pattern may reflect who posts publicly rather than a meaningful investor segment.
provisional_cards.unknown: Age, income stability and source of money stay unknown unless the person states them.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. Collect explicitly stated income pattern, source of funds, age or influence alongside first-year actions and outcomes; leave unstated attributes unknown.

provisional_cards.title: Which unmet needs deserve investigation?

working_reading.text: A Coin writer reports a missing due-date payment link, an inconsistent next-instalment display and no visible modify/cancel tab, then asks for help. A need for clearer status or control discovery is a hypothesis; the source does not establish the current option, payment outcome or Groww fit.

provisional_cards.rival_to_check: An apparent unmet need may already be met by an existing control that the writer did not know about.
provisional_cards.unknown: Repeated complaint language is a need hypothesis until the desired progress and current alternative are checked.
provisional_cards.next_decision: Review these proposed leads. For each candidate need, capture the desired progress, current workaround, reported consequence and a counterexample where existing controls sufficed.

candidates.name: What does the first payment set up?
candidates.observed: A first-SIP writer reported cancelling the initial buy while unsure when the next payment would occur.
candidates.consequence: The initial order was reportedly cancelled; the recurring SIP and later payment outcomes are unknown.
candidates.pathway: A misunderstood schedule could affect an intended contribution, but this account does not establish a lost scheduled instalment.
candidates.rival: Normal first-time learning or a deliberate order cancellation with no missed later payment.
candidates.next_test: Ask a first-year Groww investor to distinguish the initial buy, next due date and next successful instalment; check the actual next-payment outcome.

candidates.name: When an intended payment does not complete
candidates.observed: Adjacent-platform writers described mandate or payment-route trouble; one later reported that another UPI app worked.
candidates.consequence: Payment execution was reported as interrupted in some posts. The later update describes a workaround, not a verified scheduled SIP recovery.
candidates.pathway: If an intended scheduled instalment fails and recovery is possible, clarity about status and options may matter to a later qualifying payment.
candidates.rival: Bank or UPI rail conditions, normal processing delay, or payment recovery unrelated to the platform interface.
candidates.next_test: For one Groww due-date episode, record the intended payment, bank/mandate status, app status, action and next scheduled instalment.

candidates.name: What does pause, delete or cancel change?
candidates.observed: Writers asked about or acted on pause, delete, initial-order cancellation and stopping SIP transactions; later contribution or redemption states were not established.
candidates.consequence: A paused SIP was reportedly deleted in one account; whether holdings changed or future payments stopped is unknown.
candidates.pathway: Understanding control consequences could help an investor carry out an informed choice; continuation is not automatically the right outcome.
candidates.rival: The controls may behave correctly and the writer may simply be seeking confirmation after a valid choice.
candidates.next_test: Observe a safe, non-transactional Groww task: explain what each control changes, then verify the current product behaviour.

candidates.name: What happens when payment trust weakens?
candidates.observed: An adjacent-platform writer reported pausing investments amid redemption and support concerns.
candidates.consequence: A reported investment pause is not proof that a scheduled SIP stopped or that support caused it.
candidates.pathway: Unresolved status or support may change an investor’s next choice, but its link to a qualifying month-12 payment is unmeasured.
candidates.rival: The pause may reflect circumstances outside the app, and the support question may never have affected a payment.
candidates.next_test: Ask what the investor sought from support, what response arrived, what choice followed, and what happened to the next due payment.

preliminary_comparison.limitation: Unscored research leads from unreviewed, adjacent or eligibility-unknown accounts; not selected Groww problems.
